India's National Immunization Schedule (NIS)
A Simple, Age-Wise Vaccine Reference Chart
For Parents, Caregivers, and Community Health Workers
Overview
Vaccination protects children from serious diseases that can cause severe illness, disability, or death. The Government of India runs the Universal Immunization Programme (UIP), which follows the National Immunization Schedule (NIS). This schedule tells parents and health workers exactly which vaccine should be given at which age, from the day a child is born until the age of 16 years. Pregnant women are also given a vaccine to protect the mother and newborn from tetanus.
All vaccines listed in this schedule are given free of cost at government health facilities. This document lists the schedule age group by age group, along with the vaccine name and the disease it prevents, written in simple language.
Vaccine Schedule by Age Group
At Birth (within the first few hours to days)
6 Weeks
10 Weeks
14 Weeks
9 Months (9–12 months)
16–24 Months
5–6 Years
10 Years
16 Years
* Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccine (PCV) is currently available under the government programme in selected states and districts, and is being expanded across the country in a phased manner.
** The Japanese Encephalitis (JE) vaccine is given only in areas identified as endemic for the disease, based on guidance from local health authorities.
Where to Get These Vaccines Free of Cost
All vaccines listed in the National Immunization Schedule are provided completely free of cost at government health facilities across India. Parents and caregivers can visit any of the following centres:
Anganwadi Centres, on fixed immunization days announced by the local ASHA or Anganwadi worker.
Sub-Centres and Health and Wellness Centres in the village or locality.
Primary Health Centres (PHC) and Community Health Centres (CHC).
District Hospitals and Government Medical Colleges.
Parents should keep the child's immunization card safely and carry it at every visit, as it records which vaccines have already been given and when the next dose is due. If a scheduled visit is missed, the remaining doses can still be completed later; families should consult the nearest ASHA worker, ANM, or PHC for guidance rather than skipping the vaccine altogether.
Source Basis
This chart is based on general public immunization guidelines published by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), Government of India, and the National Health Mission (NHM). No specific data has been copied directly; the schedule has been rewritten in simple language for easy understanding. Vaccine availability under the government programme may vary slightly by state, and families should confirm current details with their local health facility.
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India (MoHFW) — www.mohfw.gov.in
National Health Mission (NHM), Government of India — Universal Immunization Programme — www.nhm.gov.in
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare — Immunization Handbook for Medical Officers
This content is for general awareness only and does not replace professional medical advice.
